p0.text: Sunlight contains all colors, but as it passes through Earth's atmosphere, shorter wavelengths like blue and violet are scattered far more strongly by nitrogen and oxygen molecules than longer wavelengths like red. We perceive the sky as blue rather than violet because our eyes are more sensitive to blue light and the Sun emits less violet to begin with.

p7.text:
• A solitary lighthouse keeper named Elias, stationed on a remote rocky island, discovers a weathered glass bottle wedged in the tide pools one stormy morning, containing a faded letter written in a language he cannot read but which bears the seal of a ship that sank over a century ago.

• Obsessed with uncovering the letter's meaning, Elias travels to the mainland and consults a retired linguist, who deciphers the message as a desperate plea from a dying sailor asking that his final words of love be delivered to his daughter in a coastal village—words that were never sent.

• Elias tracks down the sailor's great-great-granddaughter, an elderly woman living in that same village, and reads the letter aloud to her; she weeps, thanks him, and from that day forward
